tldr: Magentic-One is a generalist multi-agent system that autonomously solves complex tasks through coordinated planning, execution, and recovery loops across specialized agents (Orchestrator, WebSurfer, FileSurfer, Coder, ComputerTerminal).
contributions: A novel multi-agent architecture with dynamic routing between specialized agents driven by an Orchestrator
A nested-loop workflow combining outer-loop task planning with inner-loop execution and recovery
AutoGenBench, a standalone evaluation tool using freshly initialized Docker containers for independent, safe task evaluation
Evaluation on three benchmarks: GAIA, AssistantBench, and WebArena
methods: Magentic-One uses five agents: an Orchestrator that manages task decomposition, planning, and coordination; a WebSurfer for browser-based tasks using set-of-marks prompting; a FileSurfer for handling various file types via a markdown-based preview; a Coder for writing and debugging Python code; and a ComputerTerminal for deterministic execution of code and shell commands. The system employs a nested-loop workflow where an outer loop maintains a task ledger with facts, guesses, and plans, while an inner loop creates progress ledgers by answering five questions (task completion, looping detection, progress, next agent, next instruction). A stall counter with threshold ≤2 triggers recovery and plan revision when agents get stuck.
results: Evaluated on GAIA (465 multi-modal QA pairs), AssistantBench (214 QA pairs), and WebArena (812 tasks). GAIA is split into 165 validation and 300 test questions with string-matching evaluation. AssistantBench has 33 validation and 181 test questions with both exact and soft accuracy metrics. WebArena was split by MD5 hash into 422 validation tasks (hash starting with 0-7) and 390 test tasks, evaluated only once on the test set.
limitations: The system operates within a time budget (e.g., 25 minutes) which may constrain complex tasks
Education guesses are used as fallbacks when agents get stuck or run out of time, indicating potential reliability gaps
WebArena has no formal validation/test split provided by the dataset, requiring the authors to develop their own
Agents must clear their contexts and reset states after each plan update, potentially losing information across iterations
Initial systems evaluated on tasks requiring library installation are disadvantaged compared to later runs since Docker containers are fresh per task
